children: Wheat for December delivery rose 0.9% Tuesday on the Chicago Board of Trade to $7.28 1/2 a bushel as winter planting got off to a slow start and optimism faded for a Russia-Ukraine truce.
Soybeans for November delivery rose 1.1% to $13.18 3/4 a bushel.
Corn for December delivery rose 0.5% to $5.35 3/4 a bushel.

Hopes Dashed: Grain futures shook off early weakness as expectations dimmed for a truce between Russia and Ukraine after the two sides exchanged strikes overnight despite President Trump's assertion that they had agreed to stop attacks on energy targets. The prospect of such a halt prompted hopes that any agreement could extend to attacks on shipping in the Black Sea, which has affected grain exports.

Crop Progress: The U.S. corn crop was in 57% good/excellent condition this week, up from 56% the week before but down from 67% this time last year, according to the USDA's latest report. The corn harvest was 8% complete compared with 7% a year ago. "The widespread heat waves seen to finish the growing season have certainly sped up maturity, but scattered heavy rains across the Midwest in the last week ultimately kept somewhat of a lid on progress at the national level," Mike Castle of StoneX said in a note. Soybeans were 58% good/excellent, with 6% harvested. That's double the five-year average of 3%, "again reflecting the rapid maturation due to recent excessive heat," Castle said.

Behind on Planting: U.S. winter wheat planting at 8% is below the five-year average of 12% for this time of year, which raises concerns about a second consecutive year of low winter wheat production, analysts at Rabobank said in a note. On the bearish side, global inventories are rising amid logistics constraints, and increasing stocks in Ukraine and Russia "could lead to a substantial carryover into the next marketing year," they added.

Ethanol Exports: The U.S. exported a record 2.2 billion gallons of ethanol in 2025 worth $4.7 billion, and exports of the biofuel were up 12% in the first half of this year by volume and 21% by value, the USDA said in a report, noting growing global demand and reduced competition from Brazil. Several unknowns could alter the trajectory. Brazil may recover export market share if its production outpaces domestic consumption growth, while any change in U.S. policy, such as a nationwide E15 mandate, could limit exportable supply and push up prices. Demand may also rise further as countries respond to higher energy prices caused by the Middle East conflict. "Ethanol prices have not spiked like oil and gasoline, giving ethanol an advantage and encouraging higher blending as a method to reduce prices at the pump," the USDA said.
The EIA will release its Weekly Petroleum Status Update report at 10:30 a.m. ET Wednesday.
The USDA will release its weekly export sales report at 8:30 a.m. ET Thursday.
The USDA will release its monthly Cattle on Feed report at 3 p.m. ET Friday.
The CFTC will release its weekly Commitment of Traders report at 3:30 p.m. ET Friday.
